sports.headline: India pile up athletics medals, but gold remains elusive India won six athletics medals on Monday to take its overall tally to 19 at the Asian Games, but the elusive gold remained out of reach. Day 10 wrap: India add 8 medals on rain-hit day in Nagoya Asian Games 2026: India collected eight medals on a rain-hit Day 10 in Nagoya, with athletics contributing six and Esha Singh adding shooting silver. The day also brought Vithya Ramraj's national record, a washed-out cricket quarter-final and boxing progress into the semifinals.

Records are meant to be broken: PT Usha's emotional tribute as Vithya makes history Vithya Ramraj broke PT Usha's 42-year-old national record in the women's 400m hurdles, clocking 54.75s to win bronze at the Asian Games 2026. Usha congratulated the Indian hurdler after the record-breaking run.

Vithya Ramraj breaks PT Usha's record, wins 400m hurdles bronze Vithya Ramraj has finally moved past PT Usha's 42-year-old national record in the 400m hurdles, clocking a personal best of 54.75 seconds to win bronze at the Asian Games in Nagoya. The landmark run also gave her a second medal at these Games.

Esha Singh survives 4 shoot-offs to win pistol silver at Asian Games Esha Singh won silver in the women's 25m pistol event at the Asian Games after surviving four shoot-offs before losing the final tie-breaker to China's Xiao Jiaruixuan. The medal came after Esha qualified eighth and fought her way into the gold-medal contest.

Pincky Balhara becomes India's Kurash legend with bronze medal in Nagoya Pincky Balhara has put Kurash back on the map, eight years after her historic performance in the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta. With her second Asian Games medal, Pincky has cemented her status as a legend of the game.

A key highlight on the opening day was an exhibition women's polo match organised by the Ladakh Authority. The match took place at Ladakh's historic horse polo ground, where polo was played during the era of Maharaja Gulab Singh and Maharaja Ranbir Singh. Featuring female riders from various parts of the country playing by centuries-old rules, the match drew visitors, including international tourists from Dubai, who praised the players' passion and highlighted the event as a significant step towards women's empowerment.
